PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Increased screening risk with nuchal translucency >4mm at <14 weeks gestation
Ultrasound Findings: Skin edema and atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) noted
Gestational Age: <14 weeks

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured chorionic villi to detect aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. Multiple short tandem repeat (STR) markers were assessed for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S11, D21S1437, D21S1409, D21S1435, D21S1442, D21S1411
- Sex chromosomes: AMELX/Y, X22, DXYS218, SRY

LIMITATIONS
This test may not detect low-level mosaicism (<20%), segmental imbalances, balanced rearrangements, or polyploidy. Results should be confirmed by conventional karyotyping.

RESULTS

ABNORMAL RESULT DETECTED

Molecular Karyotype: rsa(X,13,18)x2,(21)x3

Chromosome 21: TRISOMY 21 DETECTED
Informative markers:
- D21S11: Triallelic pattern (1:1:1 ratio)
- D21S1437: Triallelic pattern (1:1:1 ratio)
- D21S1409: Diallelic pattern (2:1 ratio)
- D21S1435: Triallelic pattern (1:1:1 ratio)
- D21S1442: Diallelic pattern (2:1 ratio)
- D21S1411: Diallelic pattern (2:1 ratio)

Chromosome 13: Normal female pattern
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns

Chromosome 18: Normal female pattern
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns

Sex Chromosomes: Female (XX)
AMELX: Single peak consistent with XX
SRY: Absent

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis has detected trisomy 21 in the fetal sample. Six informative chromosome 21 markers confirmed the presence of three copies of chromosome 21, consistent with Down syndrome. The normal complement for chromosomes 13 and 18 was confirmed. The sex chromosome pattern indicates a female fetus.

The trisomy 21 finding is consistent with the ultrasound abnormalities reported, including increased nuchal translucency, skin edema, and atrioventricular septal defect, which are commonly associated with Down syndrome.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Follow-up karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to confirm this result and exclude any additional chromosomal abnormalities not detectable by QF-PCR
2. Genetic counseling should be offered to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
3. Further detailed ultrasound examination may be considered to assess for additional features of Down syndrome

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
